title: Filtered 2-colimits of categories
statement:
Let $I$ be a preordered set (in the applications a directed one) and $(\mathcal C_i)_{i\in I}$
categories. A *cocone of categories* with vertex a category $\mathcal D$ consists of

- transition functors $T_{ij}\colon\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$ for $i\le j$,
- functors $\Phi_i\colon\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D$, and
- natural isomorphisms $\theta_{ij}\colon\Phi_j\circ T_{ij}\cong\Phi_i$ for $i\le j$.

No coherence between the transition functors is required. The cocone *is a filtered 2-colimit*
if it satisfies:

- **(Obj)** every object of $\mathcal D$ is isomorphic to $\Phi_i(x)$ for some $i\in I$ and
  $x\in\mathcal C_i$;
- **(Hom-surj)** for all $i,j\in I$, $x\in\mathcal C_i$, $y\in\mathcal C_j$ and every morphism
  $\varphi\colon\Phi_i(x)\to\Phi_j(y)$ there are $k\ge i,j$ and a morphism
  $g\colon T_{ik}x\to T_{jk}y$ in $\mathcal C_k$ with
  $\varphi=\theta_{jk,y}\circ\Phi_k(g)\circ\theta_{ik,x}^{-1}$;
- **(Hom-inj)** for every $k\in I$ and morphisms $g,g'\colon x\to y$ in $\mathcal C_k$ with
  $\Phi_k(g)=\Phi_k(g')$ there is $k'\ge k$ with $T_{kk'}(g)=T_{kk'}(g')$.

In particular, in a filtered 2-colimit every object of $\mathcal D$ comes from a finite stage,
and morphisms of $\mathcal C_k$ identified in $\mathcal D$ are identified at a finite stage.
This is a property of ordinary categories and functors; no higher categories are involved.

proof.text: The data in the statement are exactly a cocone of categories as defined in [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-cocone]: the isomorphism component has source $\Phi_j(T_{ij}x)$ and target $\Phi_i(x)$. On these data impose the conjunction (Obj), (Hom-surj), (Hom-inj) of [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-conditions]. This defines a predicate without imposing directedness, identities or composition constraints on the transition functors. The formula in (Hom-surj) is typed because $\theta_{ik,x}^{-1}$ goes from $\Phi_i(x)$ to $\Phi_k(T_{ik}x)$ and $\theta_{jk,y}$ goes from $\Phi_k(T_{jk}y)$ to $\Phi_j(y)$.

source.place: Definition: cocone data and three conditions

proof.text: For the two concluding assertions, fix an object $d$ of $\mathcal D$ and take its witnesses $i,x$ and $d\cong\Phi_i(x)$ from (Obj). Next fix $k$, $x,y\in\mathcal C_k$ and $g,g^{\prime}:x\to y$ whose images under $\Phi_k$ agree; (Hom-inj) supplies $k^{\prime}\ge k$ and equality of their images under $T_{kk^{\prime}}$. These are precisely the asserted finite-stage conclusions. Neither implication uses coherence or directedness.

source.place: Final paragraph; direct elimination of (Obj) and (Hom-inj)

proof.text: For the separate interpretation by a comparison category, assume additionally that $I$ is directed and that the cocone has the coherent normalized structure explicitly specified in [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-model]. That node gives the category of pairs $\mathcal C_\infty$, its filtered Hom-set colimits and its comparison functor $\Phi$. Under these same hypotheses [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-characterization] identifies essential surjectivity of $\Phi$ with (Obj), fullness with (Hom-surj), and faithfulness with (Hom-inj), and concludes that their conjunction is equivalent to $\Phi$ being an equivalence. This interpretation concerns the additional coherent normalized case; it is not a hypothesis of the predicate defined above.
